sections.what_is_sinusitis: Inflammation or swelling of the tissue lining the sinuses is called sinusitis. Various bacteria, viruses, and fungi are responsible for this disease. Naturally sinuses are filled with air but in this disease sinuses are blocked and filled with various germs and fluids. These microbes grow and result in infections.
sections.types_of_sinusitis:
ACUTE SINUSITIS – Acute sinusitis usually last for 4 weeks. Various symptoms of this type are cold, facial pain and stuffy nose. 
 SUB-ACUTE SINUSITIS – In sub-acute sinusitis inflammation and underlying symptoms lasts for 4 to 8 weeks. 
 CHRONIC SINUSITIS – In chronic sinusitis all the symptoms and inflammation last for more than 8 weeks. 
 RECURRENT SINUSITIS – It is a type of sinusitis in which various attacks occur within a year.

sections.causes_of_sinusitis:
Viral infections – common cold is mostly the cause of sinusitis. 
 Bacterial infections – infection in upper respiratory tract persists long for 10 or more days then it is more likely to be caused by bacterial infections. 
 Fungal infections – weakness and various abnormalities are observed if it is caused due to fungal infection. 

 Other causes may include allergies, nasal polyp, nasal tumors, deviated nasal septum, tooth infections and various other medical conditions.
